text: If your ship got hit by a cannonball, you'd actually be one of the lucky ones.
In the 1700s, the Navy's round shot would smash through a pirate ship's wall and turn
it into a storm of splinters that tore through half the crew.
The pirates couldn't afford proper ammo, so they fired back with Langerage, which is a fancy
But the Navy had a nastier idea called Hot Shot.
They shoveled cannonballs into a furnace until they glowed red, carried them over with giant
tongs, and dropped them in behind a soaking wet plug so the gunpowder wouldn't go off
The ball buried itself deep in the pirate ship's hull, and a few minutes later, the
whole ship lit up from the inside like a giant lantern.
Not to be outdone, the pirates fired back with the carcass.
A hollow cannonball packed with burning tar and punched full of holes, so it spat fire
the whole way over and turned the entire navy ship into a torch.
Eventually, ships advanced from wood to iron, and the fireballs just bounced off.
So America built the Rodman gun, a cannon that fired a single ball weighing over a thousand
pounds, made to punch a hole in an iron warship big enough to sink it in one shot.
